Company relationships/Source notes

Data provenance and method

This page documents the dataset and transformations used by the company relationship explorer. The research snapshot was exported on October 20, 2026; the article and interface were redesigned on November 9, 2026.

The historical graph

The export contains 20 company records and a curated subset of relationship records from the existing research workspace. It is not a complete supplier database. Profile assertions, filing candidates, and reviewed filing links remain distinct.

  • stock_graph/profiles.py: company descriptions and shared economic drivers. Profiles were reconstructed retrospectively and intended to describe 2010-era structure.
  • stock_graph/results/edges.csv: relationship types, supplier/customer direction, economic explanations, and historical-change flags.
  • stock_graph/results/filing_relationships/candidates.csv: Apple/Intel filing candidates and dated source references.
  • stock_graph/results/filing_relationships/reviewed_edges.csv: reviewed parent-level SkyWest/Delta and Republic/Delta links through regional-carrier subsidiaries.
  • stock_graph/docs/FILING_RELATIONSHIP_PILOT.md: review decisions, rule-development sample, and validation limits.

These paths identify the original workspace records; they are not hosted routes. The website serves the curated JSON export, which includes source references for the filing-backed records. It does not include licensed price panels or option quotes.

Tracing a scenario

Supply arrows run from supplier to customer. A demand scenario follows those links backward; a supply-disruption scenario follows them forward. An unweighted breadth-first search returns companies reachable within one or two hops, counting each company once at its shortest distance.

Only supply links transmit these scenarios. Competitor, shared-driver, and input-cost links can be inspected as context. The evidence and relationship filters apply before the trace. Neighborhood mode shows the focal company, its direct neighbors, and any additional companies reached by a trace.

The algorithm identifies paths, not effects. It uses no estimated coefficients, contract weights, probabilities, causal signs, or expected returns. Node locations are an editorial layout. Equal node sizes do not imply equal business exposure.

Reading the evidence

A profile assertion has not been independently established by the attached filing pilot. An Intel component mention in an Apple filing remains a candidate for a direct purchasing link. The reviewed Delta links are parent-level interpretations based on named subsidiaries, not observations of current contracts.

A disclosure date is not the contract’s start date. Missing end dates do not establish continuing validity. The small filing pilot was used to design its extraction rules, so review on that sample does not establish performance on unseen firms.

Design and typography

The article layout was informed by Optiver’s research blog: a headline, category and date, short introduction, a feature figure, section navigation, and a readable article column. All research text, diagrams, and branding here are specific to this project. The site is not affiliated with Optiver.

Optiver’s inspected stylesheet uses Roboto for body text and Century Expanded LT Std for headlines. This project bundles the open-source Roboto family and uses locally available Century fonts when present, with bundled Libre Baskerville as the distributable headline fallback. It does not bundle Optiver’s commercial headline font, custom Opticode font, logo, article copy, or images.

Font files and their SIL Open Font License texts are included under assets/fonts/. There are no remote font, analytics, or application API calls.

Run or publish

The complete website is the dist/ directory. It runs on a static HTTP server with no dependencies or build step:

python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory dist

The source download includes a GitHub Pages workflow. Configure Pages to use GitHub Actions and push the project to a repository whose default branch is main. The workflow checks the local sources and publishes dist/. Repository subpaths work because application assets and data URLs are relative.
